scenario_explanation: Over a 90-Sol simulation, modifying conditions from Scenario A (Sleep=6.0h, Recovery=1.0h, Workload=80.0%, Exercise=45.0m, Cabin pCO2=3.8 mmHg) to Scenario B (Sleep=8.0h, Recovery=2.5h, Workload=55.0%, Exercise=120.0m, Cabin pCO2=2.0 mmHg) shifts end-of-mission Composite Readiness from 43.1% to 89.1% (+46.0%). Specifically, HRV RMSSD shifts by +32.1 ms, femoral BMD loss changes from -2.84% to -0.93% (+1.91%), and the SANS neuro-ocular proxy shifts from 58.1% to 30.1% (-28.0%). Note: Sol 0 reflects literature-anchored PUBLIC DATA baseline values; Sols 1–90 are parametric SIMULATED OUTPUTS.

equations_and_assumptions.scientific_disclaimer: RESEARCH PROTOTYPE DISCLAIMER: This system is an exploratory mathematical digital-twin research simulator and NOT a clinically validated astronaut physiological twin or medical diagnostic device. All long-horizon trajectories beyond empirical observation windows are parametric simulations governed by the equations and assumptions documented below.
equations_and_assumptions.governing_hybrid_state_equation: x_{t+1} = f_mech(x_t, u, e; theta)   [this build: mechanistic ODE only; the ML residual term w_ML(t) * g_ML(...) is NOT applied, so every Sol > 0 is a parametric SIMULATION]

state_variables.S_t: Homeostatic Sleep Pressure / Fatigue Index in [0, 100]% (lower is better rested)
state_variables.RMSSD_t: Autonomic Vagal Tone (HRV RMSSD in ms; higher indicates stronger parasympathetic recovery)
state_variables.BMD_delta_pct_t: Cumulative Weight-Bearing Bone Mineral Density Change (% relative to L-3 pre-flight)
state_variables.SANS_proxy_t: Neuro-Ocular / Cephalad Fluid Congestion Risk Proxy in [0, 100]%

sleep_duration_hrs.supporting_source: PhysioNet MMASH (sleep.csv) & Sleep-EDFx Borbely Two-Process Priors

recovery_duration_hrs.supporting_source: Post-exertion parasympathetic rebound time constant (MMASH Activity.csv + RR.csv)

workload_intensity_pct.supporting_source: UCI WESAD & MMASH ENMO physical/cognitive strain coupling

exercise_duration_min.supporting_source: NASA OSDR OSD-51 (WISE-2005 Bed Rest Exercise Countermeasure) & NASA HRP BMD priors

cabin_co2_mmhg.unit: mmHg partial pressure (1 mmHg ≈ 1,316 ppm at 760 mmHg)
cabin_co2_mmhg.supporting_source: NASA OSDR EDA ISS Cabin CO2 Telemetry & PhysioNet CVES Cerebral CO2 Reactivity

1_sleep_and_fatigue_dynamics.assumption: Discrete daily Borbely-style homeostatic balance: wake time and workload above the reference schedule (16 h wake, 55% load, 7.5 h sleep, 1.5 h recovery) accumulate sleep pressure; cabin pCO2 > 2.5 mmHg adds a sleep-fragmentation penalty.

2_autonomic_hrv_rmssd_dynamics.assumption: Vagal tone relaxes toward a load-dependent target: suppressed by workload and sleep pressure, restored by recovery blocks and up to 90 min/day of conditioning.

3_musculoskeletal_bmd_dynamics.assumption: 0.0433 %/day ~= 1.3 %/month unmitigated weight-bearing BMD loss (within the NASA HRP 1.0-1.5 %/month range); 120 min/day exercise offsets ~76% of that loss.

4_neuro_ocular_sans_proxy_dynamics.assumption: Exponential cephalad fluid-shift saturation (tau = 18 sols) plus a power-law hypercapnia term above 2.0 mmHg. This is a risk PROXY, not a measured optic-disc metric.

limitations: 1. Population-Level Priors: Mechanistic rate constants represent published group means and do not capture patient-specific genetic or anatomical variance (e.g., optic nerve sheath anatomy in SANS).
2. Absence of Continuous In-Flight Wearable Validation: Open NASA repositories (OSDR) release discrete blood/omics panels rather than continuous in-flight wearable waveforms.
3. First-Order Coupling Approximation: Cross-subsystem interactions (such as hypercapnia affecting sleep fragmentation and cerebral blood flow) are modeled via first-order linear/power-law terms.
